module: Real astronomical sky driven by the level's TimeOfDay. The clock (time, play, dayLength) and the observer's place/date (latitude, longitude, year, month, day) come from the TimeOfDay; the extension positions the sun, the moon (size and phase) and the orientation of the star field at that same instant (ScatterSky object). It also handles shooting stars, solar eclipses, a per-level sky profile (atmosphere, bodies) and a detail card on hovering stars/constellations. A modder uses it to change the place, the date, the moon size, display grids or replace the sky computation (setDriver).
usage:
core_celestial.setLocation(47.0, 8.0)   -- latitude, longitude in degrees
core_celestial.setDate(2026, 8, 12)    -- Perseids peak
core_celestial.setMoonScale(0.08)
core_celestial.setDisplayOption('constellationLines', true)
local ecl = core_celestial.findNextSolarEclipse() -- {year, month, day, time} or nil
notes: Stays loaded between levels (setExtensionUnloadMode manual). At each level, the caches are emptied and the sky profile is re-read (onClientPostStartMission) from tod.celestialProfile (bare name -> /art/skies/profiles/<name>.json, or path starting with /) otherwise from celestial.json in the level folder; at the end of the level the profile is forgotten.
Positioning is done in onPreRender (not onUpdate) because the C++ TimeOfDay advances its time between the two: no one-frame lag.
Default values if the TimeOfDay has no place/date: latitude 47, longitude 8, 2026-06-20. Default moon size 0.05; north offset 0; azimuthSign 1 (set to -1 if the sky is mirrored east-west).

The astronomical models (Schlyter's Sun and Moon, refraction, lunar parallax, civil time zone + daylight saving time) are contained in this file; setTimezone(nil) deduces the time zone from the longitude.
Shooting star presets: default (real calendar), low = 10, moderate = 30, high = 120 meteors/min.

setDisplayOption keys -> ScatterSky fields: constellationLines -> constellationsEnabled, constellationLabels -> constellationNamesEnabled, horizonGrid -> gridEnabled, equatorialGrid -> equatorialGridEnabled, meridianGrid -> meridianEnabled, moonGrid -> moonPathEnabled.
Hovering sends the guihook "CelestialHover" when the target changes; selection is limited to about 16 Hz and only if the sky is visible.
The extracted field `hover` is described here; the file's other local functions (computations, star maps, ~1000 lines) are not exported.

hover.desc: Public settings of the hover detail card, modifiable without forking the file: dist (16 m in front of the camera), starHeight 4.6, constHeight 2.5, rightFrac 0.82, downFrac 0.10, tilt -0.22, res 2 (texture supersampling), starPickDeg 1.5 (angular distance to pick a star), constPickDeg 6 (to pick a constellation), shimmerDist 40, shimmerRadiusFrac 0.025, shimmerColor {r,g,b}, leaderColor {r,g,b,a}, and the replacement functions starTemplate(), constTemplate(), starVars(meta), constVars(id). After replacing a *Template, call refreshHoverCards().

setEnabled.desc: Enables or disables the real astronomical sky (enabled by default); the transition is applied on the next frame.

on.desc: true = real sky; false = restores the level's original night ambiance

isEnabled.desc: Tells whether the real astronomical sky is enabled.

findNextSolarEclipse.desc: Looks for the next solar eclipse visible from the level observer's location, starting from the current TimeOfDay instant.

returns.desc: {year, month, day, time} at the eclipse maximum, nil if none in the search range or no TimeOfDay

setDriver.desc: Replaces the sky computation every frame. fn(ctx) receives the prefilled real sky values (ctx.sunAz/sunEl, ctx.bodies, ctx.star*, ctx.meteor*, ctx.time/jd/lst/lat/lon) and a utility ctx.altAz(raDeg, decDeg); it modifies them to move the sky. nil restores the built-in computation.

fn.desc: function fn(ctx); any non-function value is treated as nil

getDriver.desc: Returns the current custom sky driver.

returns.desc: driver or nil if the built-in computation is used

setHoverEnabled.desc: Enables the detail card on hovering stars (the UI overlay enables it while shown). Disabling clears the last result.

returns.desc: card of the last hover or nil

refreshHoverCards.desc: Destroys the hover cards so they are rebuilt from M.hover on the next hover (to call after replacing a *Template).

setNorthOffset.desc: Offsets true north relative to the world's +Y axis.

setAzimuthSign.desc: Reverses the east-west direction of the sky if the sun/stars appear mirrored.

setMoonScale.desc: Changes the moon size (applied immediately if the real sky is active).

s.desc: scale; 0.05 by default, the levels' default (~0.2) is huge

setMeteorTest.desc: Debug: forces a heavy meteor shower even out of season.

setMeteorTestRate.desc: Debug: sets the shooting star rate and enables test mode.

setMeteorRatePreset.desc: Chooses a shooting star rate preset.

preset.desc: default (real calendar), low (10), moderate (30), high (120); nil = default; unknown value = no effect

setDisplayOption.desc: Enables/disables a sky display layer (see notes for valid keys). No effect if no ScatterSky or unknown key.

key.desc: constellationLines, constellationLabels, horizonGrid, equatorialGrid, meridianGrid, moonGrid

returns.desc: {hasSky=boolean, constellationLines=..., ...}; only hasSky if there is no sky

setLocation.desc: Writes latitude/longitude to the level's TimeOfDay (source of truth). Does nothing without a TimeOfDay.

setDate.desc: Writes year/month/day to the level's TimeOfDay; nil arguments are ignored.

setTimezone.desc: Civil time zone of the observer. A level can also set tod.utcOffset / tod.dstRule directly.

stdOffsetHours.desc: standard UTC offset in hours; nil = deduced from the longitude

rule.desc: daylight saving rule: auto, eu, us, au, none; nil = unchanged

loadProfile.desc: Loads or replaces the sky profile (atmosphere, bodies). The atmosphere block is pushed to ScatterSky on the next frame.

profile.desc: path of a JSON or already decoded table

returns.desc: false if the profile is neither a table nor a readable JSON
enabled, hoverEnabled, northOffsetDeg, azimuthSign, moonScale, latitude, longitude, year, month, day, time, meteor{name,test,ratePreset,rate,showerFraction}, display

selftest.desc: Self-test of the math part (JD, sun, moon, refraction, parallax, time zone, meteors, eclipses). Raises an assertion error on a mismatch.

onPreRender.desc: Per-frame hook: applies the profile's atmosphere, then computes the position of the sun, moon and stars from the TimeOfDay and updates hovering; or restores the original sky if disabled.

onExtensionLoaded.desc: Hook: sets the extension to manual unloading.

onClientPostStartMission.desc: Hook: a level has just been loaded; empties the caches and reloads the sky profile.

onClientEndMission.desc: Hook: end of the level; empties the caches and forgets the profile.

onLanguageChanged.desc: Hook: language change; rebuilds the name atlas and the hover cards (free if nothing changes).

onReloadLocales.desc: Hook: hot reload of the language files; same effect as onLanguageChanged.
